title: Flag code for a previous visit
statement: Let $M$ be a finite-state binary Turing machine with $k$ work tapes, let $m,t\in\mathbb{N}$, and let $\tau$ be one of its work tapes. Form the Boolean word of length $t$ whose entry at $s<t$ is true exactly when the head of tape $\tau$, after $s$ steps on the all-zero input of length $m$, is at the same position as after $t$ steps. The code of the index immediately before the word's last true entry (or the empty word if there is none) equals the optional-time code of the largest such $s<t$, with the code empty if no such $s$ exists.
replaced: For every oblivious machine, reference length $m$, time $t$, and work tape $\tau$, the last-visit code of the flag word testing, for each $s < t$, whether the work position at $s$ equals the position at $t$, is exactly the optional-time code of the public last-visit value; the time is in canonical binary.
